title: Summer flow gave no clear added March forecast gain at three Arctic gauges in 29 winters from 1981 to 2011
abstract: We tested whether July-September flow improves March forecasts after prior March, November and time are known. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 approved daily data at Ob, Lena and Yenisey, with earlier-year fits and 29 common winters from 1981 to 2011. Adding summer mean flow increased equal-river mean squared log-flow error by 1.21%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for error reduction was -11.79% to 4.19%. Last-25-winter fits also gave no clear gain. A secondary no-time test increased error by 3.65%. The main test gives no clear added skill. It does not show that summer storage has no winter effect. Short records, regulation, revised data, one linear term and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Original code, aggregate scores, source hashes, an arithmetic audit and a figure support reproduction. External source and record-level tables remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Adding summer flow gave no clear main-test gain. Points show equal-river mean error reduction. Bars show conditional 95% three-year block intervals. Positive values mean lower error.
